ledger.claim: The driver's own GPS trace never places him inside the 120 m arrival radius for LARGE_VENUE at any point: his minimum distance to the pickup pin across the whole trace is 258.2 m, more than twice the radius, and he recorded zero qualifying in-geofence fixes. POL-NS-02's arrival test therefore fails outright and POL-NS-01 limb (b) cannot be satisfied.

The driver's 'I'm Here' tap at 12:30:36 was a false arrival marker: at that moment his trace places him 258.2 m from the pin, and his recorded speeds on the approach run to 62.9 km/h, far above the 15 km/h motion threshold. Under POL-NS-05 the marker does not start the waiting clock, and because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, limb (ii) applies: the fee is refunded in full, no compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver.

Even on the driver's own account the waiting period was never served: the free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), the wait timer started at 12:30:38 and the driver cancelled at 12:34:59, but the effective in-geofence dwell computed under POL-NS-02 is 0.0 seconds against a required minimum of 180 seconds for LARGE_VENUE — a shortfall of 180 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present.

The rider did everything the platform asks of a waiting rider: at 12:30:56 she sent a locating message naming her exact position — 'im at the main entrance next to the taxi stand, block A' — and the driver's only response was 'ok' at 12:31:26, 30 seconds later, with no in-app call recorded anywhere in trip_record.in_app_calls. Her own track places her within the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius for all 54 of her fixes (max distance 19.9 m, all at 0 km/h), so limb (c) is affirmatively satisfied. POL-NS-04 exonerates her and refunds the fee in full with no driver compensation.

The driver's stationary position was outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin (minimum distance 258.2 m), which is the wrong-entrance case of POL-NS-03: the fee is refunded to the rider in full. On fault, the rider named her entrance in chat ('main entrance next to the taxi stand, block A') and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, so under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation.

The fare ledger confirms the money actually moved against the rider: the cancellation-fee line is SGD 4.50, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the full contested amount of SGD 4.50 is still being carried by the rider and is the sum that must be returned.

The driver's own profile shows a trailing-30-day no-show termination count of 1 against 92 completed trips — a rate of roughly 0.011, far below the 0.08 threshold — so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and nothing in this record supports the driver retaining any part of the fee. I note that the lifetime counter prior_no_show_flags (2) is not the field POL-NS-07 reads and I do not rely on it.

ledger.claim: The trip record shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 12:30:36 and the platform's own wait timer started two seconds later, so the arrival event required by POL-NS-01(a) exists on the record.
The driver's GPS trace runs 91 fixes at a 10 second cadence with 100 percent coverage and no gaps, so the trace is complete and unimpaired for the arrival and dwell tests.

The rider's own device track places the rider within 12.95 to 19.90 metres of the pickup pin across 54 fixes, all stationary, so the rider was physically at the pickup point throughout the waiting window and the driver's cancellation was not a case of a rider stranded elsewhere.

The rider's message at 12:30:56 named the main entrance next to the taxi stand at block A, and the driver replied 'ok' at 12:31:26, so the driver acknowledged the rider's stated location and had the information needed to move to it before cancelling at 12:34:59.

The fare ledger shows the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 charged and no refund issued, and the driver's compensation on that fee computes to SGD 3.60 at the 80 percent rate, so the money the driver is owed is fixed and the charge is presently standing.

The anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip: the driver's no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by 92 completed trips in 30 days is far below the 0.08 rate, so compensation is not withheld.

The driver's own trace shows a minimum distance of 258.21 metres from the pickup pin and zero qualifying in-geofence fixes, so the driver never entered the 120 metre LARGE_VENUE arrival radius and POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails on the driver's own evidence. I concede this point: the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the SGD 4.50.

The driver's stationary position at 258.21 metres from the pin falls outside the arrival radius but within the 400 metre ceiling of POL-NS-03, so this is a wrong-entrance case and the fault allocation turns on the chat log: the rider named the main entrance at block A and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, so under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation.

The driver's trace shows zero in-geofence intervals and a longest qualifying run of 0 seconds against the 180 second minimum dwell for this zone class, so the waiting-period shortfall under POL-NS-06 is 180 seconds and the full refund stands with no driver compensation payable.
The traffic advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload, so POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable and no advisory can be asserted to accumulate dwell or to excuse the shortfall.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this dispute is decided on the driver's own GPS trace. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 12:30:36 and the platform's wait timer ran, but under POL-NS-02 the driver is deemed to have arrived only if the trace shows at least 3 consecutive fixes inside the arrival radius for the zone class. Tampines Mall is a LARGE_VENUE, so that radius is 120 m (fee_schedule.arrival_radius_m). The driver's trace (91 fixes, 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps) never places him closer than 258.2 m to the pickup pin and records zero qualifying in-geofence fixes. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails, and with limb (c) unserved (0 seconds of in-geofence dwell against the 180-second free waiting period in trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec) the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is not chargeable. The driver's closest position, 258.2 m, lies outside the arrival radius but within the 400 m ceiling of POL-NS-03, so fault is allocated from the chat log. At 12:30:56 the rider sent 'im at the main entrance next to the taxi stand, block A' — her own position — and the driver replied only 'ok' at 12:31:26 and did not move to that entrance before cancelling at 12:34:59. Under POL-NS-03(i) the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation. The rider is refunded the full SGD 4.50 (fare ledger cancellation_fee = SGD 4.50, total_charged = SGD 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd = 0.00). Driver's counsel: the trace is complete (accepted); the 'arrived' event exists (accepted, but limb (a) alone does not carry POL-NS-01); the rider was within 12.95–19.90 m of the pin (accepted); compensation computes to SGD 3.60 under POL-NS-07 (rejected — POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not); the anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d = 1 against completed_trips_30d = 92, rate 0.011, both under the POL-NS-07 thresholds), which is accepted but moot because no compensation is due at all. Rider's counsel: POL-NS-04 is rejected — the driver replied 'ok' 30 seconds after the rider's message, well inside the 120-second window, so that clause does not apply whatever the reply said; the false-arrival argument under POL-NS-05 is rejected — 258.2 m is inside the 300 m mark and the driver was stationary there, a driver stationary within 300 m but outside the arrival radius is decided under POL-NS-03, and no fix shows him travelling at 15 km/h or more at the arrival timestamp, so no false-arrival referral is produced; the 180-second POL-NS-06 shortfall is accepted and consistent with this result, though POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unavailable because EV-ADVIS-02712-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). Two advisory claims (one from each side) were discarded at the mechanical citation check for citing that 0.0-weight artifact without naming its issue code, as the audit record shows. The driver's statement that he 'was at the pickup as shown on the map' is not supported by his own trace and does not displace it; the coordinates decide. No escalation: confidence 0.95 is above the 0.70 floor; no artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d) carries a deciding fact; no POL-NS-09(c) or (d) trigger is met; and the profile fields the parties cited are either properly cited for their own tests or, in the one case where a context-only lifetime counter was mentioned, expressly not relied on. The deciding artifacts all carry weight 1.0, so no disclosure discount applies. The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is within the SGD 8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so the refund executes on issue. Either party may appeal once under POL-GEN-04 within 30 days.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
